utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, good morning, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I'd like to introduce to the Chamber Simeon Dukic from Macedonia who is joining us during this session and is working on our case as a legal intern. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Mr. President, you asked us to look quickly at the Martic submission. I wanted to advise the Court that the Prosecution would not take a position on that; however, we did think it worth noting that it appears that the Rules provide for review by the President, and for the record the general provisions are found in Rule 19, 19(A), and 33(A), and the more specific provision that appears to relate to this is Rule 44(B).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You will come back separately as regards Milan Babic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless there's anything further, we'll bring in the witness. In the meantime, we'll admit the 65 ter 24790.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I want to -- I'll let you get settled first, sir.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At paragraph 34 of your statement you discuss in passing the question of a Bijeljina Crisis Staff. I want to suggest to you, Mr. Simic, that there was a Bijeljina Crisis Staff and it was not as non-existent or inconsequential as your statement might suggest. I'll put two things to you first and then ask you a question. The first is that this Trial Chamber has, in fact, received a fax, that is, a copy of a fax that was sent at the time on April 1st from the Bijeljina Crisis Staff to the SDS Main Board, reporting on the situation at that time, that's P2626. And I also want to take a look at what people in Bijeljina were saying at the time, were saying contemporaneously, and for that we can look at a portion of events that were captured on video, so I'd ask to turn to 65 ter 40144 to the clips found at -- beginning at 1.36.19, and for the interpreters that's found at page 2 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will this document be 262 [as interpreted] be shown to the witness or is he supposed to trust you just because you told him so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Tieger referred to for your reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We're going to see a number of Crisis Staff references during the course of this examination. If the witness wants to turn to that document, we can certainly do so when we've reviewed the rest of the material. We can run that clip. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a video of events on the 2nd of April, 1992, in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "At the moment we liberated the centre of the town, the snipers are in the surrounding skyscrapers, but we will neutralise them certainly to the end of the day. Allegedly this is the notorious Handzar division. How much truth is there in this? "The members of the paramilitary units tried to take the town during the previous two nights and to block off the Serbian people so they could terrorise it, but with the quick action of our people and our Crisis Staff we have thwarted that attempt, and I repeat that the civilian part of town will be under our control until the end of the day. "Mr. Rakic, this is from the Crisis Staff? "Yes, when we were sitting in the Crisis Staff, there was combat going on outside."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, as we can see people are referring to the Crisis Staff at the time of the events at the beginning of April 1992. I told you about some of the evidence the Court has already received. Is it still your position -- well, is it your position, sir, that there was no Crisis Staff and that you don't know what Crisis Staff these people in the video are referring to?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: P2626, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the 65 ter number of that video, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's 40144, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it to be found on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry 40144D. And, Mr. President, while we're waiting for the document to come up, a portion of that video is already in evidence as P5587 and we'll be seeing that portion again in addition to a number of other clips. So at the end we'll try to identify where those are and amalgamate them in a sensible manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. The document on the screen, Mr. Simic, is a report from the Bijeljina Crisis Staff to the SDS Main Board and the date is 1 April 1992. Indeed, it's a report on the situation as of 2000 hours on 1 April. Okay.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The video-clip that you played, I don't see by anything that anyone is from Bijeljina or that this occurred in Bijeljina. I have no idea. I've never seen that at all. What's the evidence that there was a Crisis Staff, the fact that some people are talking in a TV show? That a Crisis Staff existed in Bijeljina, but what were the decisions that it made? What was it doing? There are no such documents or no such activities. And as for this report, it's not signed. Who were the members of the Crisis Staff and what was the decision that it made. If this is just some reporting --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, Mr. Simic, I'm not asking you to argue your position. I just want to hear what your position is and if we can continue with that evidence. Now, you asked about other evidence. Do you know who Predrag Jeseric was? Do you remember the chief of the SJB in Bijeljina in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I remember Predrag Jeseric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, in a report sent directly and personally to Mico Stanisic, Mr. Jeseric said there was a Crisis Staff and that it grew into the War Presidency you acknowledge being the president of. That's P2629 if we can call that up. And it's the first paragraph on page 2 of the English and it's about the seventh paragraph, so I turn to page 2 of the B/C/S as well. And Mr. Jeseric stated in this report personally to Minister Stanisic: "As a measure of precaution, the Bijeljina SO," skupstina opstina, "Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff which grew into the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly decided that classes ...," et cetera, et cetera. So Mr. Jeseric, the chief of police also understood at the time that there was a Crisis Staff, sir, and indeed it grew into the War Presidency that you were the head of. Do you still say there's no evidence and that you were unaware of any Crisis Staff, sir?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the fact that there was a War Presidency in Bijeljina is not correct, not in the period in April and thereabouts when I was the president of the Municipal Assembly. There was the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly which functioned in accordance with the Statute of the Municipal Assembly and there was also a council of the Municipal Assembly which was constituted in accordance with the documents of the Municipal Assembly. On the 1st of April I held a meeting of the National Defence Council at the barracks rather than the Crisis Staff and it was attended by the representatives of the Muslims and the Muslim-elected leaders. The Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, not the War Presidency, I emphasize, because there's not a single document of the Municipal Assembly that mentions it. Whether anyone wrote something -- because there are so many documents from the Municipal Assembly and you could have determined how the organs were called and what they were doing. The Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina began to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, let's not get hung up on the -- that was -- let's not get hung up on the distinction between War Presidency and Presidency. Mr. Jeseric called it a Presidency, it's called Presidency in the documents, so I accept that we'll use that designation from here on out. But let's get more to the point --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Fine. So we've seen the locals at the time who understood there was a Crisis Staff. We've seen the document reporting by the Crisis Staff. We see Mr. Jesuric's acknowledgement that there was a Crisis Staff that grew into the Presidency. You also mention in your statement Mrs. Plavsic's visit to Bijeljina, Mr. Simic, and the fact is that Mrs. Plavsic knew there was a Crisis Staff because she went to see -- she asked to see and she went to see the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a reference to that. Where did we see the locals talking about the Crisis Staff? The witness said that these were not any people from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's the Prosecution's position. I'm happy to tender the entire document which will make it crystal clear that that took place on Bijeljina. In fact, based on that objection, I'm going to tender that entire document when we're completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Tieger was referring to Exhibit P2626. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Simic, that you reference Mrs. Plavsic's visit and the fact is that Mrs. Plavsic asked to see and did go to see the Bijeljina Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did they meet and who were the members of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's just take a look at some of the -- what we can see based on video evidence, Mr. Simic, about the Crisis Staff. First, can we have clip 1.51 -- beginning at 1.51.12. And, Mr. President, that's a portion of 40144D that overlaps with 5587 and 5588.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Well, first of all, I wanted to come here -- no, I wanted to come here first and to contact the Crisis Staff directly, first myself, and then we all talked together, and now we are expecting them and then I will also go to the barracks. "Are you familiar at all with what is going on in the barracks that they had to go there first? "No, no, I have no idea. I mean, the soldiers are in the barracks. I don't know why they would go to the barracks just to see the soldiers. Let me tell you why. I think you see that there isn't any -- I think that there are no bad intentions about this. Because we were escorted -- the police escorted us from Tuzla up until here. A military patrol escorted us to Tuzla. "I have to ask you. "So it would have been normal if I had gone to the barracks first, but since I can decided for myself, I decided to go to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian people first to meet with Mr. Arkan and with his associates here" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we stop that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Zeljko Raznatovic here. If he was the Crisis Staff and if that's what Biljana says, then perhaps, but that's not the Bijeljina Crisis staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? I'm sorry, it wasn't interpreted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. You've identified that man as Arkan; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Zeljko Raznatovic, yes. But I don't see any Crisis Staff here. Mrs. Plavsic talks about the Crisis Staff, but I would like to -- on the basis of what, who, where, what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We'll see some more, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's at -- thank you. Arkan is identified as 1.52.23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness's answer has not been recorded. The witness said if it was some Crisis Staff. It's not the municipal Crisis Staff, and this is not recorded. It wasn't the municipal Crisis Staff. It's just the transcript. Everything needs to be recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. That will be checked. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please continue to the end of this clip which is brief.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I knew that such a close meeting" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Stop there -- sorry to interrupt the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And who is depicted -- who are the two people depicted in this portion of the video at 1.52.30?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that to the left is Djoja Arsenovic, Mr. Arsenovic, of Bijeljina; and as for this, I don't know who this is, the bearded man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You don't recognise him as Goran Hadzic, the same Goran Hadzic who is currently on trial here?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they aren't -- he doesn't really look a lot like the one today. Perhaps it is Goran Hadzic. I'm not opposed to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt the interpreters. If they could just finish -- we'll finish that clip and they can just finish the last sentence they were interpreting.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Encounter first would be better without the other ones and then later we would talk with them too."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So in this portion of the video of April 2nd, 1992, Mrs. Plavsic in the span of a minute or two twice mentions the Crisis Staff, that she wanted to leave the delegation that she travelled with at the barracks and then come here where she was, first, to contact the Crisis Staff directly, and meet with Mr. Arkan and his associates and Mr. Adzic as it says here. Now, she and the others, she indicates in the latter portion of her comments, are waiting for the other members of the delegation, including Mr. Fikret Abdic to join them. So let's continue to see who arrives to join the group and who's with the group waiting to greet the other members of the delegation. That can be found beginning at 1.53.57. And before I start that, Mr. Simic, you're clear on where we are now, right, that we're about to look at another clip a few minutes -- events that took place a few moments later? Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The meeting. Fikret Abdic arrives. That's the return from the barracks? "Yes. We waited for quite a long time for them to come to this particular meeting. You will see the tension, the nervousness. Something in the air because we were not ready."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now we're back in the same room waiting for the delegation. Do you recognise this person in the forefront of the video?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not from the local administration or, I suppose, from Bijeljina. Just let me explain. All this is taking place in the building of the Municipal Assembly in Bijeljina, where I was the host, and I'm not there and the Crisis Staff is not there, at least not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who is -- 1.54.41, who is the gentleman that Mr. Abdic is greeting?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's me. I was the host there, as I said, but it wasn't the Crisis Staff. That was the building of the Municipal Assembly in Bijeljina and I had no idea what Mrs. Plavsic talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Plavsic: This is the place. Bishop Kacavenda is also coming here. Hello, how are you?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Stop -- let's return it slightly. We didn't stop it quick enough. Let's go to right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's a better picture of a younger you, right, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who is shaking Mr. Abdic's hand?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see well. Perhaps it's Ljubisa Savic, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ljubisa Savic, also known as Mauzer; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possible. He looks like him though he's much younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And who is the man in uniform immediately to the left in the photograph of --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You don't recognise --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You don't recognise General Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't. Perhaps I just met him once casually somewhere in passing. I didn't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Continue, please. That was at -- we're looking at 1.55.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Stopping here at 1.55, I don't think that was intentional but it's a good place to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We see the man you tentatively identified as Ljubisa Savic, Mauzer, talking to the general and you saw him depicted a little more clearly as the video progressed?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I just wanted to confirm, in fact, having had a better chance to look at the man in the leather -- what appears to be a leather jacket and dark hair, you confirm that was Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed, please. [Video-clip played].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "How was your journey? "Fine, excellent, since 6.00 this morning. I just shaved and straight to work. First it was Mostar, then from Mostar to Derventa, and from Derventa and back to Tuzla. "And the other general, 2nd Military District command, why couldn't he come? "No, he could not for official reasons, business. "Business? "Since I have been put in charge of this meeting, I'll just -- a little -- but we have to wait for the bishop, wait for the bishop. "No need. The representative of our Crisis Staff will explain how it was envisaged -- "No, no, I'm not going to explain the situation. About the protocol, about the way that we would hold this meeting, you understand? "All right."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were unable --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we know who it was that said", No, no, I'm not going to explain the situation"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm just going to return to that, Mr. President, because you couldn't hear the voices -- first of all, the transcript identifies it as being, but I was going to return so we could hear the actual video and ask the witness that very question. So can we return to approximately 1.56.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Simic, I'll ask you to listen to the two voices.

utterances.speaker: MRS. PLAVSIC SAYS
utterances.text: "Since I have been put in charge of this meeting we'll have to wait for the bishop." And then we hear another voice say: "No need, the representative of our Crisis Staff," and I believe there's another reference to "and the representative of the SAO government will explain how it was envisaged." And I want you to listen to both of those portions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Since I've been put in charge of this meeting , I'll just" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot overlap so we can hear the actual video and audiotape because once they start to translate we no longer hear the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it possible -- because I'm not able to upload the transcript myself because there's some error message, but does the transcript show the identity of the speakers?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It does, Mr. President, but as you'll see there's a -- in this particular instance the speaker is off-screen and so it's a little more tentative. Apart from that, I think it's fair to do this and I will simply note that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think it's a useful exercise. But for the interpreters, I'll note they've already interpreted this portion. We have it on the record. Now we're just going to play it so the witness can hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could -- yeah, let's move it back maybe 10 seconds or so so we can hear the beginning of what Mrs. Plavsic says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You recognise the speaker who is talking to Mrs. Plavsic and telling her there's no need to wait for the bishop? That's you; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is Mr. Ljubisa Savic, as far as I can tell. I'm not sure. It's not me, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Although you just told us you were hosting the meeting?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the host and I greeted the guests, but I didn't speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So you think it's Mr. Savic and you're not sure it's you? Is that what you told us? Because I'm looking for a transcript correction here based on what I understand was said.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So, Mr. Simic, you've seen the fax from the Crisis Staff, you've seen the people at the time --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not see the fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We put that on the screen in front of you, sir, and I'm not going to do it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember the fax that you say about it? You can't see the signature at all. There's no name. It was sent in the name of Crisis Staff to the SDS Main Board. Do you remember having seen it a moment ago, that he referred to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, that's -- all right, all right. Before that some other fax appeared in my material. I thought ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay, so you've seen that. You've seen the guys on the video earlier talking about the Crisis Staff and the actions taken by the Crisis Staff. You've seen the reference by Mr. Jeseric to the Crisis Staff. You've seen that Mrs. Plavsic came and wanted to see the Crisis Staff. And now we see you here at a meeting where the Crisis Staff is mentioned. Do you still maintain that the Crisis Staff was inconsequential and essentially didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that the Crisis Staff did not exist. According to your evidence it may be interpreted that General Jankovic and Fikret Abdic were members of the Crisis Staff too because they were present there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We've seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In this regard can I draw your attention -- your comment on transcript page 10, lines from 7 to 11. So you said in the course of questioning the witness: "... Mrs. Plavsic in the span of a minute or two twice mentions the Crisis Staff, that she wanted to leave the delegation that she travelled with at the barracks and then come here where she was first to contact the Crisis Staff directly, and meet with Mr. Arkan and his associates." So did you mean she contacted Crisis Staff first and then meet with Mr. Arkan?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't intend to say more than was indicated by Mrs. Plavsic in the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but if you take a look at transcript page 8, lines 6 to 9, what Mrs. Plavsic allegedly said is this: "I have decided to go to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian people first to meet with Mr. Arkan ..." So it sounds as if Mr. Arkan seems to be a member of the Crisis Staff. Could you clarify with the transcript. Shall we hear again the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We can hear it again, but I don't -- first of all, the punctuation in the transcript is slightly different and telling, and that is: I decided to go to the Crisis Staff. In other words, she could have gone to the barracks, she says, but she decided to go to the Crisis Staff first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To meet with Mr. Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And his associates here. So to meet with Mr. Arkan and others. So you can -- if you want to interpret it as Arkan being part of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The point I wanted to make is that it's very clear that Mrs. Plavsic, in addition to other evidence that we've seen, is aware of a Crisis Staff and wants to go meet the members -- meet with the Crisis Staff rather than go to the barracks with the other members of the delegation initially. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Please, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I'd also say of course in a case like this no single piece of evidence is read without looking at the other evidence, and that's why I'm referring to many pieces of evidence that reflect the existence and nature of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But I wanted to turn now to the persons we --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? May I ask the Prosecution to give us Mauzer's words literally transcribed, what he exactly said in this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I don't accept that those are -- that that's Mauzer. And yes, I'm happy to have that listened to again and again. As I said, when we listened to it carefully we heard the words of that speaker --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- let's proceed. It's in the transcript or we can hear it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've been thinking myself about this transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because I was not able to see it. Can we upload the transcript then? Because of that upgrade probably I'm not able to open -- see the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm also not able to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I mean, that's a technical matter. We can listen to over and over. As everyone knows, the more you listen to it, the more you may hear. As I said, it's reflected as -- the portion reflected as unintelligible in the transcript, I think one can clearly hear that that speaker is saying the representative of our Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just indicate the page that was shown to the witness. Who was in charge and let's wait for the bishop, what page was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's at page 8, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reflection of the speaker in the words attributed to this witness, I don't believe it should be -- should be attributed to this witness in the transcript if, in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. But we -- what's the basis of the evidence in the transcript attributing it to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's -- well, we'll not discuss it here, but it's for the Prosecutor to clarify. Let me -- can I see it? Is it -- is this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, page -- it's page -- also page 2 of 5588.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we know what was redacted here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know, this is really -- Mr. Karadzic was in court. This came in in that fashion because of -- because the entirety of the -- this is the reference that was played in court. He knows that very well. I'm aware of the fact that both Mr. Robinson and Mr. Karadzic are very unhappy with this evidence, but I really resent these constant disruptions for no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Do we see the part which was attributed to Mr. Simic? Yes, I think I'm seeing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, if I can remind the Court, the Court was minded at that moment to simply tender the transcript, and it was the Prosecution that suggested we give the witness a chance to hear it and offer whatever comment he could. So I don't know how we could have been more fair about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, we saw Mr. Arkan -- we saw Arkan, Mr. Raznatovic, in these videos. Now, just by way of background, Arkan was a well-known, indeed famous, figure who was, I think we could say fairly, loved or thought highly of by the Serbs and feared, in particular, by the Croats as a result of events in Croatia during the war. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that you've exaggerated it a bit. As far as Bijeljina is concerned, he was well-known, but I don't know that he was particularly liked or popular before these events, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But he was feared by non-Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot interpret that now how they felt. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You're the president of the municipality, you're meeting with members of -- representatives of the Muslim community. You're presumably meeting with members of the Bijeljina community at all times. And you have no -- and you're on the border of Croatia. You're monitoring events of the war in Croatia, as you told us in your statement, and yet you have no idea about how the members of your community feel at all about this well-known but controversial figure. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. I'm telling you that I think that the citizens of Bijeljina did not think about Arkan until the 1st of April. I don't see any reason why they should be afraid, why they should have any fear. I have no such feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to -- just very quickly I'll try this. I'm looking at an article of December 16th, 1991, by the "Los Angeles Times," referring, among other things -- and that's 65 ter 24787, referring to, among other things, Arkan's renowned as a guerilla leader who leads the Arkan's Tigers who claimed to fight fascism and take no prisoners; or 24788, an "Associated Press" article the next month, in January of 1992, again referring to Arkan's fame and the fact that he is adored by the Serbian press. So it's your testimony, sir, that although Arkan's renown and the controversial nature of that renown appears to have been known in many, many parts of the globe, that you and Bijeljina really were oblivious to Arkan before April 1st?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that we didn't know. I said that citizens did not think about Arkan. I believe that the citizens of Bijeljina do not read this - what was the name? - "Los Angeles Times," or what was the newspaper that you mentioned? I think that the citizens of Bijeljina have absolutely no contact with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know what, Mr. Simic, I don't know if that's supposed to be serious, but you're not really claiming to this Court, are you, that the people of Bijeljina could only have become aware of Arkan and thought about Arkan if they had happened to have a copy of the "Los Angeles Times"?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the evidence that you are putting before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Simic. I was pointing out how widespread his fame was and suggesting to you that right across the border from Croatia where those events were taking place, the man who came in on April 1st -- who came in at that point would have been someone that people in Bijeljina just might have been thinking of. But let's move on. You said people weren't thinking --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, we can't move on after Mr. Tieger makes a speech or a submission without asking a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, fair enough. Would you like to answer or to comment on Mr. Tieger's comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that people knew about Arkan but not to that extent and he did not have the kind of significance that the Prosecutor is referring to. In my view - and you will judge the extent to which I am right - media popularity and presentation starts after these events in Bijeljina. I think that that is how it was, but the Prosecution has some other information. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mention April 1st as the day that people started worrying about Arkan. Let's call up 65 ter 15576 and turn to the third page of the English, and that's the heading that begins "17th Corps." This is a report of the command of the 2nd Military District to the Main Staff of the SFRY getting reports from various corps. 17th Corps is headed by General Jankovic. And it states as follows: "During the 31st of March and 1st of April, 1992, there was an escalation of conflict on the territory of Bijeljina municipality" --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Under -- at the bottom of the page you're now looking at.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Second paragraph: "During the non-confirmed information, Arkan's men entered Bijeljina in the part of the city which is populated by Muslims. Barricades were set and the passage through the city is blocked. Explosions and gun-fire can be heard from the city." So that conforms to your reference to when people started thinking about Arkan, that is on April 1st; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I see that in the report, but I also see that at 1400 hours a meeting was scheduled of the organs of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6209, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So when you speak in paragraph 27 of your statement about the SDS -- SDA president on the 1st of April not wanting to lift the barricades immediately but to have UN observers come in first, that's the context, right, that Arkan is already present and people know about it?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day before that, the night before that, the conflict started. On the second day we held the meeting at 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to make a habit when I can of noting when precisely the allocated time has expired, but I trust that given the fact that I'm very much focused on key issues and have been throughout that the Court will extend that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. But for planning purposes, how much longer would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm guessing about -- don't have that much more, but I think about 20 minutes. Certainly I'll finish in this session but I'm hoping to finish within 20, as I have a limited amount of stuff to cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could try to finish in 15 minutes. Do your best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That -- that might be tough, but I'll do my best, Mr. President. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The fact is, Mr. Simic, that Arkan was there and he was there because the Bijeljina municipal authorities invited him in; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You keep trying. The fact is that Arkan was there, but how do you get this information that he was invited by the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We'll return to the video and return to the clip at 1.39.25, please. Oh, I'm sorry, it's -- 1.39.50 is where the clip is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's Arkan again, right, and that's Arkan saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it interpreted? We didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Mr. President, that's true. The interpreters do have that transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell us the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we play again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Well, number one, number one, the Serb volunteer guard has come here after being invited by the Territorial Defence and the Serb people of Semberija and Bijeljina, and of course we came to our people's rescue."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. That's Arkan saying that he was invited and that's why he showed up. In fact, Mr. Simic, you refer in one of your documents to the fact that you did invite armed groups and uniformed -- armed and uniformed groups, but that there were other armed and uniformed groups who were uninvited that you were -- thought should then leave. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I mean, I don't know what kind of practice this is, to keep putting Arkan here. He says that he was invited by the Serb people and the Territorial Defence. He is not mentioning the Municipal Assembly and the authorities of the town of Bijeljina. Please play it again and see if I'm right. You keep adding things that were not said. And in which document did I invite paramilitaries to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which -- let me ask you this question: Which armed and uniformed groups came to Bijeljina by way of invitation and which armed and uniformed groups came without being invited by the legal organs of Bijeljina municipality? So which armed groups were invited by the legal organs of the Bijeljina municipality?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No armed groups came at the invitation of the municipal authorities of the town of Bijeljina --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I mean all paramilitary units are those units that were not under the command - if you mean up until the 20th of May - that were not under the control of the JNA or the command of the police. All of those are paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's turn to 1D5015, page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D2372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's not it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to return to that because the -- as a result of the upload the number seems to be changed. That is the number that came out before the transition with or the upgrade of e-court. All right. Mr. Simic, after the events in Bijeljina you were aware that there were allegations about the conduct of Arkan and, indeed, there were some extremely famous photos of Arkan and Arkan's forces in Bijeljina at the beginning of April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who made which allegations?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's just look at the photographs and see if you recognise those.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's P2919, pages 26 through 29. Next photo, please. Turn to page 26, please, the series. Maybe it's best to go to the ELMO on these things or page 28. Mr. Reid suggests it might, indeed, be better to go to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I see 28, 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It seems to be up now. Okay. So page -- and page 29, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. E-court page 28. That's page 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. That's page 30. Okay. And page 30 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What we see is page 26 on e-court. Why? We go to the last page then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those are the photos I was talking about, Mr. Simic. You've seen those before; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the one that was before it was published in some book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay, the one immediately before that, the one that depicts the three people on the ground, two guys with guns and caps -- there you go, that one right there. That's the one you're talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a book published in our region featuring this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you're aware that these photos were published and distributed essentially worldwide and roughly at the time and since; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know then that they were published throughout the world and I don't know it now. I don't even know whether they are from Bijeljina. Is there any identification of these people? What is to confirm the location?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It doesn't take much to go to Haviv's -- Mr. Ron Haviv's web site or the web site of a -- called iconic photographs, which means photographs that are particularly famous, and see the description of those photos including the explanation of how they were taken by Mr. Haviv and indeed including the fact that he came to Bijeljina afterwards and talked to people about the photographs and makes it very clear that these are photographs he took of Arkan's figures in Bijeljina at the beginning of April 1992. So is it your testimony that as the president of the municipality at that time and a continuing resident of Bijeljina you had no awareness that these were photographs of Bijeljina involving Arkan's forces?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about these photographs at that time. I said I'd seen them in a book published in Bosnia. I can't recognise these people because I don't know Arkan's men and I don't know the victims, so how could I comment on either?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. If I have time I'm going to play you a video of Arkan acknowledging that those are his forces when he sees the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But first I want to return to what is apparently D01445, second page. Second page of that, please --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is a one-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Then let's put this on the ELMO, please. That was 1D15015, as we were notified by the Defence, and then they removed these exhibits which were supposed to be associated at the last minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a conclusion from the Presidency of the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly of 29 May 1992 signed by you, Mr. Simic, referring to the behaviour of armed and uniformed groups and individuals who have come from the territory outside Bijeljina municipality without being invited by the legal organs and notes are causing disruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We are -- I was told that this document is in e-court. I would like the Registrar to let us know the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D15015, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can we upload it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The documents are on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you -- no. Why do we see a different document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The document that was just shown is -- okay, this is not the document I'm referring to and it's not the document that is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now we are seeing -- what I see from my personal computer is different from what I see in the public monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. And on -- okay. Well, this is -- on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- is the document I referred to and was reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as I said, Mr. Simic, that's a conclusion from 29 May 1992 of the Presidency of the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly signed by you referring to groups and armed and uniformed groups and individuals who came without being invited and then going on to say: " The Presidency, therefore, prohibits any individuals or groups not invited by the legal organs from being engaged as instructors or in any other capacity ...," and so on and so on. So that's a reference, Mr. Simic, is it not, to groups that were both invited and not invited, right, by the legal organs of the Bijeljina municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we see here the groups invited, reference to the groups invited?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It doesn't specify the groups unless you're asking, Mr. President, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That's for you to answer the question, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This conclusion of 25th May -- 29th May has nothing to do with these documents and photographs of the 1st and 2nd of April. There's a two-month difference. And after those problematic days in April we had problems in the area of the municipality and we asked that all groups or individuals presenting themselves as volunteers or whatever be placed at the command of those who were competent in our area, that was the East Bosnia Corps and the public security station. That was our conclusion and that conclusion was two months after these events. But we in the municipality made our decision already on the 8th of April concerning events of the 1st and the 2nd of April. So this document has nothing to do with the April events in Bijeljina. And I can comment on this order of this 25th of June. I'm glad that we made such good decisions and conclusions in that period. This order of the 25th of June relates to a prohibition of a paramilitary or a parapolice unit under the command of some Davidovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Wait a minute, excuse me, excuse me, Mr. Karadzic can get into this if he wants. This document is not on at the moment. I have limited time. I want to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it of six-page document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Which one, may I ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was only aware of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think what --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What we saw is page 2, according to my e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Right. I am only aware of two pages in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, we'll admit them. [Overlapping speakers] We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P6210, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I could have addressed this at the end, but I think it's probably sensible to admit the entirety of this video 40144, otherwise there's at least one other clip I was going to get to, but if it's going to be subsumed under the entirety of the video which seems to be something that the accused was interested in as well, then I would simply do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you could give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would object to the admission of the whole video and believe that only those parts that are discussed in court should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Then let's turn to 1.56 -- to clip at 1.56.25.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We saw Mauzer on the -- that is, Ljubisa Savic on the video, Mr. Simic. He came to Bijeljina with his -- and established the Serbian National Guard -- or, excuse me, he established a Serbian National Guard, that is, the forces that were involved -- were among the forces that were involved in Bijeljina at the beginning of April pursuant to a decision of the government of SAO Majevica and Semberija; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that military unit was not formed before the 1st of April. It was formed after the April events.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's just look at that clip real quick.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The reporter: ... the representative of the Crisis Staff of -- the Crisis Staff of SAO Semberija and Majevica who co-ordinated the struggle. The fighting has finished. The town is free. "Savic: The town is free finally. At 1.03 [as interpreted] we placed all those who have weapons under our control."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The transcript -- while the transcript said -- in -- Ljubisa Savic being the representative of the Crisis Staff, our transcript does not reflect it. Do you confirm that, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection, sir, about the --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Okay. But what is the date? Is it the 2nd or the 3rd?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a portion of the video that was taken on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do we know that? How do we know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We know it -- that's why I wanted to admit the entirety of the video, once the Defence has and they can review it and see very clearly what the -- how the video is dated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Last thing I want to cover with you, sir, is the portion of your statement that refers to normalisation of life and work in Bijeljina after the events of early April, and I just want to cover a few things that you did to supposedly normalise life in Bijeljina. First of all, you replaced the TO commander, the Muslim TO commander, you've indicated in an earlier part of your statement, with the new Serbian commander Blagoje Gavrilovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I did not -- excuse me. It's not I who did that. It was the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina over which I presided and I signed the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly was reduced to 70 deputies, which was conveniently almost exactly the number of Serb deputies; right?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's only at the end of June 1992. I don't know what you're interested in. The Assembly made a statutory decision on the 25th or the 26th of June, 1992, concerning the number of deputies, probably those in attendance, and that's when I resigned and I stopped being the president of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So you confirm that on -- and I'm looking at 1D105, an article that's a session on June 25th, an article states the Assembly shall consist of 70 deputies, and I'm also looking at 1D15011, which indicates the election results and it indicates from the ranks of Serbs 69 deputies. So that's what happened in June, correct, that the Municipal Assembly was essentially reduced to its Serbian deputies? You have to answer audibly yes or no.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said so. You have that decision of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, it's called statutory decision, I believe. It was made at an Assembly meeting. It's no secret. Everything is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally you said about -- and I say "finally," with reference to the normalising activities, you said about renaming various portions of the town and one of those acts of normalising was to rename a square after Arkan's Serbian Volunteer Guards; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. It's not a square. It's possible that it was a street, but certainly not a square. The Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina adopted over 100 decisions in those three months. You can review all of them and see all the things that were done to normalise relations. Out of the 100 decisions you put two before me here. All of them are available concerning the normalisation of relations in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Chamber has been -- has allotted me the additional time. I appreciate it. The only additional thing I'd mention at this point is that yesterday the witness asked me about whether there was any document showing that north-eastern -- the autonomous region of North-Eastern Bosnia had been proclaimed or established before October, and in that respect I have 65 ter 17458, which discusses the proclamation of the autonomous region as reflected in an article in "Javnost." If the Court gives me time, I can present it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we call up 65 ter 17458.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, you do not oppose to the admission of the video-clips?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Was our comment acknowledged that the portions the witness did not identify, the men in masks, for example, should not be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous portions P5587 and -88 were admitted through a bar table motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's a good question, Mr. President. I don't have that information at my fingertips, although the number might suggest that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did we give the number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, the video was Exhibit P6211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yeah, it was confirmed by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed the onset of regionalisation and whether or not regionalisation only took place after the joint Assembly session on October 15th. I referred you to a number of autonomous regions that were proclaimed prior to that, including North-East Bosnia. You asked if you could see something like that. This is an article in "Javnost," the SDS newspaper, concerning just that which states, among other things: "The new autonomous region was proclaimed in the presence of the representatives of Bijeljina, Lopare, Brcko, Ugljevik, Zvornik, Tuzla, and Kalesija municipalities." It also goes on to note that as expected the proclamation of the new region in Bijeljina has also caused negative reactions by the other parties' representatives who described it as illegal, illegitimate, et cetera. So does this refresh your recollection, Mr. Simic, that there was considerable activity towards regionalisation prior to the joint Assembly session of October 15th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am trying to use official documents of the competent institutions. The Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina took the decision to accede to the region on the 25th October, I believe, 25th October 1991. The Assembly of the region of North-Eastern Bosnia was made and promulgated in the Official Gazette of the region. What kind of evidence is a newspaper article when we have official documents of the competent authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me try to parse that out for just a moment before we adjourn, sir. First of all, "Javnost" is the SDS newspaper; correct? Well, you don't know that either?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that more official than a document from the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina? This is not a document. It's a printed medium.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, you tried to tell this Chamber that nothing happened, that all of regionalisation was about a reaction to what happened on October 15th. I showed you -- I referred you to an evidence this Court already has and now I'm showing you a document which says -- it's dated the -- about the 28th of September, 1991, well before October 15th that shows that activity was taking place about regionalisation well before October 15th. The question is not how long it took you in Bijeljina to perfect the process and sign on to the -- to regionalisation. The question is whether or not regionalisation was moving forward before the date you said it was. And that's what this document indicates.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you expect me to comment? In my mind, a job was done when the decision was adopted. Whether the work on it took one year, 10, or 15, it does not matter. I don't even know how long it took.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you. And I would tender 65 ter 17458.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it you have some re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll hear it after a break. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I've been asked to indicate for the record that page 1 of what was admitted as P6210 was already admitted as D1445 and page 2 was already admitted as D1442.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What page was it that we admitted as P6210?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I -- my recollection of P6210 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we -- [overlapping speakers] -- I'm sorry, I overlapped. So the crux of it is we don't need to admit it separately?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But for the -- sorry, but -- so it's being -- it's -- for the record so we know what's being referred to, that should clarify, although it -- I presume -- I'm presuming that 1445 and 1442 are both one-page documents so that ends any potential ambiguity, but we should check that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I would just like to take the opportunity to introduce to the Chamber Anze Mocilnik from Slovenia who is one of our legal interns working on our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, your submission was confirmed by the Registry so we will not admit P6210 separately. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We could perhaps start with the latest subjects that were covered. Can you tell us what powers in terms of defence does the municipality have and what is the president of the municipality in those terms?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it functions in a normal way, the municipality only has the jurisdiction through the secretariat of the people's defence at the time to provide logistical support for the manning of units, recruitment, mobilisation, and so on, that is to say the administrative procedures. And when a state of war is declared, then it has some more specific authorities in terms of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And does the municipality have its defence council and its Territorial Defence, and what are the authorities and powers of the municipality and the president of the municipality in those terms?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is, or rather, there was at the time a municipal Territorial Defence staff. It directed practically the Territorial Defence units. The Assembly appointed the commander of the TO staff. The Presidency of the municipality, according to the municipality statute, would take over the jurisdictions of the Municipal Assembly if the Municipal Assembly cannot be convened. That's according to the statute of the municipality. That's how things were at the time. For whatever reasons not just reasons of war the Presidency would have those authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In which capacity did you hold a meeting in the barracks on the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of April we held a meeting of the council of people's defence of the municipality of Bijeljina and I convened the meeting after a statement I issued appealing to the citizens on the local radio station. I could not see that in the documents that were presented to me. The document -- I could actually see from the documents that a meeting was held at 1400 hours and the document also lists who attended the meeting and what was discussed during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is the president of the council for national defence in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the president of the council for national defence of the municipality; that is to say I was the president of the Municipal Assembly at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When and under which circumstances are Crisis Staffs to be established as municipal organs and who is to be the president? Who signs its documents?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents should be signed by the president of the Crisis Staff. I cannot remember that in the -- in the Assembly documents such a possibility was provided, that is to say the possibility of establishing a Crisis Staff, that something like that was envisaged by any of the documents of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if there had been, for example, in case of floods or some other emergency situations, what Crisis Staffs be established in our parts?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the civilian protection should basically do in case of national disasters and the like. So it's possible that in those provisions some possibility of something like that is envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If a Crisis Staff had been established in this crisis would that have been something bad or unusual or unlawful?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just before you answer -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now again we're moving into some form of odd solicitation of opinions. I mean, up to now the accused has tried to elicit from this witness what he knows about the situation. Now he's posing a speculative question and asking for an opinion about whether -- well, asking for an opinion and I don't think that's appropriate under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I think the point is why would the witness lie about the existence of a Crisis Staff? There's nothing wrong with there being a Crisis Staff. That's a perfectly legitimate inquiry for Dr. Karadzic to make in response to the cross-examination on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was wondering whether it was put in a leading way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the question, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, whether if it had been formed and if it had existed and if it was working in accordance with regulations this shouldn't have been any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us something about the Municipal Assembly. As a state organ or body, who did it answer to? Who did it report to in a vertical line?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, basically to the government and Assembly of the republic, depending on specific jurisdiction. Perhaps in some areas or issues it could have been different, but this belonged to the sphere of mobilisation and All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you obliged and did you at all send reports to political parties, specifically to the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the municipality and the Municipal Assembly in this period, I did not do that nor did anyone request me -- request from me to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see once again P2626 in e-court. P02626.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As the Serbian version is hardly legible I will read out something from the English version and the interpreters will interpret it to you properly: [In English] "SDS, Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "SDS Municipal Board. "Bijeljina. "Crisis Staff. "To: SDS Main Board. "Sarajevo." [Interpretation] Could you say on the basis of this heading whose organ this is?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's written there that it's a party organ if it's the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you also tell us, please look further down, I will read again in English: [In English] "Report on the situation as at 2000 hours on 1 April 1992 in the area of Bijeljina municipality. "The interethnic conflict between the Serbs and Muslims that began yesterday evening has continued, shows signs of possibly subsiding. "A short time ago the National Defence Council of the Bijeljina municipality held a meeting at which the following conclusions were made ..." [Interpretation] And I will not read out the conclusions. Is this Crisis Staff reporting about its own conclusions or the conclusions of the Council of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's obvious from what was interpreted to me that they are forwarding the conclusions from the meeting of the Council of National Defence held at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this document any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the video-clip, page 6, line 16, it was suggested that we saw there the locals discussing the Crisis Staff. Who did you recognise in the video?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not recognise anyone. If you mean the people with Balaclavas, those who were masked, I did not recognise anyone. I have no idea where that was filmed or who was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember a man who was interviewed and not wearing a mask, did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the videos we could see Ljubisa Savic and Zeljko Raznatovic in different stages. I'm not sure what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I mean the one who was sitting in the TV studio?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you remember, on page 10, lines 10 and 11, we had a video-clip with Fikret Abdic arriving to the municipality. Who was in his escort, could you notice that by focusing on the uniforms? Who was his escort?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know these people --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not by name.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were obviously some sort of troops, army. They were the Tuzla MUP, but Fikret came to Bijeljina twice. I had reports about that. Once in the evening he tried but he didn't manage to reach the town. Public security centre Tuzla was there and I could see that he was with Jankovic, you said that it was General Jankovic and that he had come together with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In which capacity were Ms. Plavsic and Mr. Abdic visiting Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there as members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, this is the first time I heard that Ms. Plavsic came to the Municipal Assembly to meet with the Crisis Staff. As I said, I was the president of the Municipal Assembly and I welcomed there as the host and I thought that they were to meet with the government and the officials of the municipality, but obviously there were all sorts of people present on the occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 1st of April did we still have joint organs or did we recognise Bosnia as a country?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which of our formations, I mean the armed formations, wore masks, that is to say Balaclavas, such as those we saw in the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen that ever up until today such a press conference. I don't remember that I ever saw such a press conference in Bijeljina or anywhere else in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you a few questions about Mauzer. How did he start? What was his formation and what were their links with the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mauzer was an influential and important member of the local parliament and the Serbian Democratic Party, and I believe that in this period there were some slight differences within the SDS. The official position was to support Yugoslavia and the Yugoslav People's Army and that's what we did; however, some of the members - I think that they were members of the SDS - who had some doubts about the JNA and its officers and I believe that they were attempting to find some alternatives. And analysing what was going on in those days, I think that Ljubisa was the one who was trying to do this. In any case, he showed up near the radio station whether he transported them that night or in any case he had this radio set from the TO and he co-ordinated activities with various groups in the conflict. And after the conflict a special TO unit was established and he was appointed the commander of that Territorial Defence unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that unit in accordance with the law and -- actually, the Law on National Defence and is it within the system?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was. It did not exist on the 1st and 2nd of April. Perhaps it was only on the 5th and 6th that this unit was formed in a way. First it operated as a TO unit and it was only later I think, two or three months later, it became part of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the clip that was shown here and that was taken on the 3rd, Mauzer says: "Tonight until three minutes past 1.00 we placed all armed Serbs under control."
